title: Records tool organization filter drifted from the canonical catalog default
surface: records tool argument catalog and browser executor
auth_mode: signed-in; source and catalog verified, native behavior not exercised
reproduction: Run pnpm catalog:tools:drift:strict against the live tool.definition catalog.
Inspect records.organization_id and compare the local Zod schema with the live parameter.
expected: Omitted or null organization_id reads across every reachable organization; an explicit id narrows the tool. The catalog and runtime expose the same optional null default.
actual: The browser handler used z.string().nullish(), which accepted omitted/null at runtime but serialized as null|string without a default. The live tool.definition parameter uses the established scalar-string/default-null catalog convention, so the release drift gate failed.
severity: S3: catalog-contract drift blocks release; a user-visible failure was not demonstrated
priority: P1: strict tool catalog parity is a required release gate
root_cause: The recent cross-organization records handler added a new parameter without using its existing nullDefault helper. The certified tool.definition row was already consistent with the surrounding records parameters; no database change was needed.
verification_status: Live audit.summary says tool.definition certified=true with zero fails. Strict tool-DB drift passed 82/82, focused records tests passed 10/10, and the required records guide, tool catalog and DB-sourced docs regenerated. Full release checks, independent source review, and native behavior remain pending.

transition_history.reason: The release preflight found records.organization_id type and default drift.
Live DB and catalog serializer review showed the local handler omitted the existing nullDefault convention.
The local correction passed strict tool-DB drift and focused records tests; release and native verification remain open.
